visual_events.description: A locked-off medium shot shows a low L-shaped and T-junction red-brick wall built on sandy soil. Bricks are laid on edge in a staggered bond, leaving rectangular vertical cavities open along the top course and fresh grey mortar spread along the top junction bed. At the right edge of the frame, `ent_mason` steps slightly forward and gestures briefly with an empty right hand around 02.8s–03.5s before turning right to reach outside the frame.
visual_events.context_result: The wall junction structure, staggered vertical joints, exposed brick faces, and open top cavities are clearly visible and undisturbed throughout this span.

script: P001 states 'Unlike conventional brickwork, where bricks are laid flat, Rat-Trap Bond Masonry places bricks on their edge. This arrangement creates continuous hollow cavities within the wall.'
background_knowledge: In masonry construction, laying bricks on edge in a header-stretcher arrangement that encloses rectangular internal cavities is the defining geometry of Rat-Trap Bond.

claim_evidence.limits: Identified from visible bond geometry and script context; no on-screen label or spoken narration in the clip names the bond.

claim_evidence.claim: The visible hollow cavities inside the brick-on-edge wall illustrate the physical structure behind the script's claims of thermal insulation and reduced brick/mortar consumption, although thermal performance, percentage material savings, and brick crushing strength are not measured in the footage.
